notes.front: What is an automatic notch filter (ANF), and what can go wrong when you use one on CW?
notes.back: ANF, an automatic notch filter: a receiver filter used to remove interfering carriers. On CW it can remove the CW signal as well.
notes.explanation: A CW signal is itself a keyed carrier, so a filter that removes carriers automatically can take it out too.
notes.example: Like a spam filter so eager that it also deletes the message you were waiting for.
notes.evidence: What problem can occur when using an automatic notch filter (ANF) to remove interfering carriers while receiving CW signals? A. Removal of the CW signal as well as the interfering carrier

notes.front: What is impulse noise, and which receiver control removes it?
notes.back: Noise that arrives as short, sharp pulses. The pool says a noise blanker removes it, unlike broadband white noise or hum and buzz.
notes.explanation: The General pool explains how: a noise blanker reduces the receiver’s gain during each noise pulse.
notes.example: Like a string of sharp clicks on a steady hiss: a blanker targets the clicks, not the hiss.
notes.evidence: Which of the following types of noise are removed by a noise blanker? A. Broadband white noise B. Impulse noise C. Hum and buzz

notes.front: What is a brute-force filter, and where does the pool put one?
notes.back: A line filter placed in series with a device’s power leads; the pool uses one to suppress interference from a line-driven motor.
notes.explanation: It goes in the power feed, the path the pool’s answer targets.
notes.example: Like a heavy-duty sieve fitted in the supply pipe to a noisy machine.
notes.evidence: What is used to suppress radio frequency interference from a line-driven AC motor? A. A high-pass filter in series with the motor’s power leads B. A brute-force AC-line filter in series with the motor’s power leads

notes.front: What is power line noise, and can digital noise reduction help with it?
notes.back: Noise carried on or radiated from power lines. The pool lists it among the noise types digital noise reduction can often reduce.
notes.explanation: The pool’s answer is “all these choices”, so power line noise sits beside broadband white noise and ignition noise.
notes.example: Like a harsh buzz in your receiver that comes from nearby overhead power lines.
notes.evidence: Which of the following types of noise can often be reduced by a digital noise reduction? A. Broadband white noise B. Ignition noise C. Power line noise D. All these choices are correct

notes.front: What is a single point ground panel for?
notes.back: A station panel whose purpose is to ensure all lightning protectors activate at the same time.
notes.explanation: Bringing the protectors to one point makes them act together rather than one at a time.
notes.example: Like a single muster point for a building: everyone gathers in one place, so they move together.
notes.evidence: E4E14 (D) What is the purpose of a single point ground panel? A. Remove AC power in case of a short-circuit B. Prevent common-mode transients in multi-wire systems C. Eliminate air gaps between protected and non-protected circuits D. Ensure all lightning protectors activate at the same time

notes.front: Where should a station’s mains surge protector be installed?
notes.back: On the single point ground panel.
notes.explanation: That places it with the station’s other protectors, which the panel makes activate at the same time.
notes.example: Like fitting a fuse box beside the main switch rather than in a back bedroom.
notes.evidence: Where should a station AC surge protector be installed? A. At the AC service panel B. At an AC outlet C. On the single point ground panel

notes.front: Among the noise types digital noise reduction can often reduce is broadband {{c1::white}} noise.
notes.back: White.
notes.explanation: Broadband white noise is one of the three noise types the pool lists for digital noise reduction.
notes.evidence: Which of the following types of noise can often be reduced by a digital noise reduction? A. Broadband white noise

notes.front: Besides broadband white noise and power line noise, which noise does the pool say digital noise reduction can often reduce?
notes.back: Ignition noise.
notes.explanation: Ignition noise is another of the three noise types the pool lists for digital noise reduction.
notes.evidence: can often be reduced by a digital noise reduction? A. Broadband white noise B. Ignition noise

notes.front: Which fault in a thermostatically controlled device can create intermittent loud roaring or buzzing line interference?
notes.back: Arcing contacts.
notes.explanation: Arcing contacts are one of the three line-noise sources the pool lists.
notes.evidence: Which of the following can create intermittent loud roaring or buzzing AC line interference? A. Arcing contacts in a thermostatically controlled device

notes.front: Which household device in a nearby residence, when defective, can create roaring or buzzing line interference?
notes.back: A doorbell or its doorbell transformer.
notes.explanation: A defective doorbell or doorbell transformer is one of the three line-noise sources the pool lists.
notes.evidence: B. A defective doorbell or doorbell transformer inside a nearby residence

notes.front: What kind of malfunctioning display can create intermittent roaring or buzzing line interference?
notes.back: An illuminated advertising display.
notes.explanation: A malfunctioning illuminated advertising display is the third line-noise source the pool lists.
notes.evidence: C. A malfunctioning illuminated advertising display

notes.front: Common-mode currents on the {{c1::shield and conductors}} can cause a shielded cable to radiate or receive interference.
notes.back: The shield and conductors.
notes.explanation: The shield does not help when current flows on the shield and the conductors together.
notes.evidence: Common-mode currents on the shield and conductors

notes.front: You switch on the automatic notch filter to kill a steady carrier, and the weak CW station you were copying disappears too. What happened?
notes.back: The ANF removed the CW signal as well as the interfering carrier.
notes.explanation: This is the problem the pool names for an ANF used while receiving CW.
notes.evidence: Removal of the CW signal as well as the interfering carrier

notes.front: With the noise blanker on, a strong nearby station suddenly seems to be surrounded by spurious signals. What might the blanker be doing?
notes.back: Distorting the strong signal, so it appears to cause spurious emissions.
notes.explanation: This is the undesirable effect the pool names for a noise blanker: the spurious signals may be the blanker’s doing, not the station’s.
notes.evidence: Strong signals may be distorted and appear to cause spurious emissions

notes.front: Unstable modulated and unmodulated signals appear at fixed frequencies in your receiver. Which kind of equipment does the pool point to?
notes.back: Computer network equipment.
notes.explanation: The pool’s description of computer network interference is exactly unstable signals at specific frequencies.
notes.evidence: The appearance of unstable modulated or unmodulated signals at specific frequencies

notes.front: On HF you hear spurious signals made from two local amplitude-modulated broadcast stations combined. What nearby cause does the pool give?
notes.back: Corroded metal connections mixing and reradiating the broadcast signals.
notes.explanation: The pool says nearby corroded metal connections mix the broadcast signals and reradiate the products.
notes.evidence: Nearby corroded metal connections are mixing and reradiating the broadcast signals

notes.front: Your receiver shows a series of carriers at regular intervals across a wide frequency range. What does the pool name as the cause?
notes.back: Switch-mode power supplies.
notes.explanation: Evenly spaced carriers across a wide range are the pool’s signature of a switch-mode supply.
notes.evidence: What causes interference received as a series of carriers at regular intervals across a wide frequency range? A. Switch-mode power supplies

notes.front: A mobile installation picks up conducted noise from the vehicle’s battery charging system. Where does the pool put the fix?
notes.back: Ferrite chokes on the charging system leads.
notes.explanation: The noise is conducted, so the fix goes on the wiring that carries it.
notes.evidence: How can conducted noise from an automobile battery charging system be suppressed?

notes.front: What problem can occur when using an automatic notch filter (ANF) to remove interfering carriers while receiving CW signals?
notes.choices:
A) Removal of the CW signal as well as the interfering carrier
B) Any nearby signal passing through the DSP system will overwhelm the desired signal
C) Excessive ringing
D) All these choices are correct
notes.back: Removal of the CW signal as well as the interfering carrier
notes.choicesExplained: B: the pool’s problem is losing the wanted signal, not nearby signals overwhelming it. C: ringing is not the problem named. D: only A is the pool’s answer.
notes.explanation: A CW signal is itself a keyed carrier, so a filter that removes interfering carriers automatically can remove the CW signal too.
notes.evidence: What problem can occur when using an automatic notch filter (ANF) to remove interfering carriers while receiving CW signals?

notes.front: Which of the following types of noise can often be reduced by a digital noise reduction?
notes.choices:
A) Broadband white noise
B) Ignition noise
C) Power line noise
D) All these choices are correct
notes.back: All these choices are correct
notes.choicesExplained: A, B and C: each is right on its own, so the pool’s answer is all these choices.
notes.explanation: Digital noise reduction can often reduce all three: broadband white noise, ignition noise and power line noise.
notes.evidence: Which of the following types of noise can often be reduced by a digital noise reduction?

notes.front: Which of the following types of noise are removed by a noise blanker?
notes.choices:
A) Broadband white noise
B) Impulse noise
C) Hum and buzz
D) All these choices are correct
notes.back: Impulse noise
notes.choicesExplained: A: broadband white noise is a job for digital noise reduction. C: hum and buzz are not impulse noise. D: only impulse noise is the blanker’s target.
notes.explanation: A noise blanker is for impulse noise; the pool gives broadband white noise to digital noise reduction instead.
notes.evidence: Which of the following types of noise are removed by a noise blanker?

notes.front: How can conducted noise from an automobile battery charging system be suppressed?
notes.choices:
A) By installing filter capacitors in series with the alternator leads
B) By installing a noise suppression resistor and a blocking capacitor at the battery
C) By installing a high-pass filter in series with the radio’s power lead and a low-pass filter in parallel with the antenna feed line
D) By installing ferrite chokes on the charging system leads
notes.back: By installing ferrite chokes on the charging system leads
notes.choicesExplained: A: capacitors in series with the alternator leads would block the charging current. B: a resistor and blocking capacitor at the battery are not the pool’s remedy. C: filters on the radio’s power lead and feed line are not the remedy given.
notes.explanation: The noise is conducted along the charging system’s wiring, so the fix goes on those leads: ferrite chokes.
notes.evidence: How can conducted noise from an automobile battery charging system be suppressed?

notes.front: What is used to suppress radio frequency interference from a line-driven AC motor?
notes.choices:
A) A high-pass filter in series with the motor’s power leads
B) A brute-force AC-line filter in series with the motor’s power leads
C) A bypass capacitor in series with the motor’s field winding
D) A bypass choke in parallel with the motor’s field winding
notes.back: A brute-force AC-line filter in series with the motor’s power leads
notes.choicesExplained: A: a high-pass filter in series would not pass the mains supply to the motor. C and D: bypass parts on the field winding are not the pool’s remedy.
notes.explanation: The pool puts the fix in the motor’s power feed: a brute-force line filter in series with its power leads.
notes.evidence: What is used to suppress radio frequency interference from a line-driven AC motor?

notes.front: What type of electrical interference can be caused by computer network equipment?
notes.choices:
A) A loud AC hum in the audio output of your station’s receiver
B) A clicking noise at intervals of a few seconds
C) The appearance of unstable modulated or unmodulated signals at specific frequencies
D) A whining-type noise that continually pulses off and on
notes.back: The appearance of unstable modulated or unmodulated signals at specific frequencies
notes.choicesExplained: A: loud hum is not what the pool links to network equipment. B and D: clicks at intervals or a pulsing whine are not the pool’s description.
notes.explanation: Network equipment can produce unstable modulated or unmodulated signals at specific frequencies, which show up in the receiver as unwanted signals.
notes.evidence: What type of electrical interference can be caused by computer network equipment?

notes.front: Which of the following can cause shielded cables to radiate or receive interference?
notes.choices:
A) Low inductance ground connections at both ends of the shield
B) Common-mode currents on the shield and conductors
C) Use of braided shielding material
D) Tying all ground connections to a common point resulting in differential-mode currents in the shield
notes.back: Common-mode currents on the shield and conductors
notes.choicesExplained: A: low-inductance ground connections at both ends are not the cause. C: braided shielding is ordinary cable construction. D: the pool does not blame common-point grounding.
notes.explanation: The pool names common-mode currents on the shield and conductors as what makes a shielded cable radiate or receive interference.
notes.evidence: Which of the following can cause shielded cables to radiate or receive interference?

notes.front: What current flows equally on all conductors of an unshielded multiconductor cable?
notes.choices:
A) Differential-mode current
B) Common-mode current
C) Reactive current only
D) Magnetically-coupled current only
notes.back: Common-mode current
notes.choicesExplained: A: differential-mode current is the opposite case, not equal on every conductor. C and D: “reactive only” and “magnetically coupled only” do not describe equal current on all conductors.
notes.explanation: The defining feature is equality: the same current on every conductor of the cable, common to all of them.
notes.evidence: What current flows equally on all conductors of an unshielded multiconductor cable?

notes.front: What undesirable effect can occur when using a noise blanker?
notes.choices:
A) Received audio in the speech range might have an echo effect
B) The audio frequency bandwidth of the received signal might be compressed
C) Strong signals may be distorted and appear to cause spurious emissions
D) FM signals can no longer be demodulated
notes.back: Strong signals may be distorted and appear to cause spurious emissions
notes.choicesExplained: A: an echo effect is not the pool’s problem. B: it does not compress the audio bandwidth. D: FM signals can still be demodulated.
notes.explanation: A noise blanker can distort strong signals so that they appear to produce spurious emissions.
notes.evidence: What undesirable effect can occur when using a noise blanker?

notes.front: Which of the following can create intermittent loud roaring or buzzing AC line interference?
notes.choices:
A) Arcing contacts in a thermostatically controlled device
B) A defective doorbell or doorbell transformer inside a nearby residence
C) A malfunctioning illuminated advertising display
D) All these choices are correct
notes.back: All these choices are correct
notes.choicesExplained: A, B and C: each is a cause on its own, so the pool’s answer is all these choices.
notes.explanation: All three can create intermittent roaring or buzzing line interference: arcing thermostat contacts, a defective doorbell or its transformer, and a malfunctioning illuminated sign.
notes.evidence: Which of the following can create intermittent loud roaring or buzzing AC line interference?

notes.front: What could be the cause of local AM broadcast band signals combining to generate spurious signals on the MF or HF bands?
notes.choices:
A) One or more of the broadcast stations is transmitting an over-modulated signal
B) Nearby corroded metal connections are mixing and reradiating the broadcast signals
C) You are receiving skywave signals from a distant station
D) Your station receiver IF amplifier stage is overloaded
notes.back: Nearby corroded metal connections are mixing and reradiating the broadcast signals
notes.choicesExplained: A: over-modulation by one station does not combine several stations’ signals. C: distant skywave is not local signals combining. D: an overloaded IF stage is inside your receiver, but the pool points to nearby corroded connections.
notes.explanation: Corroded metal connections nearby can mix local broadcast signals and reradiate the products onto the MF or HF bands.
notes.evidence: What could be the cause of local AM broadcast band signals combining to generate spurious signals on the MF or HF bands?

notes.front: What causes interference received as a series of carriers at regular intervals across a wide frequency range?
notes.choices:
A) Switch-mode power supplies
B) Radar transmitters
C) Wireless security camera transmitters
D) Electric fences
notes.back: Switch-mode power supplies
notes.choicesExplained: B, C and D: radar, wireless security cameras and electric fences are not the pool’s cause of this pattern.
notes.explanation: Switch-mode power supplies are the pool’s cause of a series of carriers at regular intervals across a wide frequency range.
notes.evidence: What causes interference received as a series of carriers at regular intervals across a wide frequency range?

notes.front: Where should a station AC surge protector be installed?
notes.choices:
A) At the AC service panel
B) At an AC outlet
C) On the single point ground panel
D) On a ground rod outside the station
notes.back: On the single point ground panel
notes.choicesExplained: A, B and D: the service panel, an outlet and an outside ground rod are not where the pool puts it.
notes.explanation: The surge protector belongs on the single point ground panel, with the station’s other protectors.
notes.evidence: Where should a station AC surge protector be installed?

notes.front: What is the purpose of a single point ground panel?
notes.choices:
A) Remove AC power in case of a short-circuit
B) Prevent common-mode transients in multi-wire systems
C) Eliminate air gaps between protected and non-protected circuits
D) Ensure all lightning protectors activate at the same time
notes.back: Ensure all lightning protectors activate at the same time
notes.choicesExplained: A: cutting power in a short circuit is a circuit breaker’s job. B and C: preventing common-mode transients or eliminating air gaps are not the stated purpose.
notes.explanation: Its purpose, in the pool’s words, is to ensure all lightning protectors activate at the same time.
notes.evidence: What is the purpose of a single point ground panel?

notes.front: Noise blanker versus digital noise reduction: which noise does the pool assign each?
notes.back: Noise blanker: impulse noise. Digital noise reduction: often broadband white, ignition and power line noise.
notes.explanation: Pick the tool by the noise: a blanker for impulses, noise reduction for the others.
notes.evidence: Which of the following types of noise are removed by a noise blanker? A. Broadband white noise B. Impulse noise

notes.front: Brute-force filter versus ferrite chokes: which noise source does the pool pair with each?
notes.back: Brute-force filter: a line-driven motor, in series with its power leads. Ferrite chokes: a vehicle battery charging system’s leads.
notes.explanation: Both go on the leads that carry the noise; the device and its supply decide which.
notes.evidence: By installing ferrite chokes on the charging system leads

notes.front: Surge protector versus single point ground panel: what is each one’s role?
notes.back: Surge protector: protects against surges, mounted on the panel. Panel: ensures all lightning protectors activate at the same time.
notes.explanation: The panel is the meeting point; the surge protector is one of the devices mounted there.
notes.evidence: What is the purpose of a single point ground panel?
